profile.research_note:
Facility specific seeding pass 2026-09-02, batch 45 (CyrusOne missing-address campaign): matched this rows own CHI3 site code to two independent aggregator listings agreeing on a specific street address distinct from the operators other Aurora buildings.

[batch narration moved out of reading 2026-09-02] CyrusOne is a large scale data center provider headquartered in Dallas, Texas. In 2016 CyrusOne purchased the Chicago Mercantile Exchanges original Aurora, Illinois data center from CME Group for roughly 130 million dollars, with CME Group continuing to operate its Globex matching engine on site under a 15 year lease. In November 2021, KKR and Global Infrastructure Partners agreed to acquire CyrusOne in an approximately 15 billion dollar deal, taking the company private, and that acquisition closed in 2022. CyrusOne has operated as a privately held company since, a company level ownership fact this registry had not previously recorded with a citable source. This specific row, CHI3, corresponds to this operators own Aurora III campus in Aurora, Illinois, part of a three building CHI1 through CHI3 Aurora campus per the operators own current locations page. A dedicated datacentermap Aurora III Campus listing and a datacenterHawk Aurora III Building 1 listing, both fetched fresh this session, agree on 2725 Bilter Road, Aurora, Illinois as this facilitys street address, distinct from the CHI1 and CHI2 buildings on the nearby Diehl Road.

reading.body:
CyrusOne CHI3 is a 450,000 square foot data center building in Aurora, Illinois, part of a three-building campus on Bilter Road. The operator has published 114 MW of total IT capacity across the entire Aurora campus, but has not published a figure specific to this building, so its individual contribution to Illinois' data center footprint cannot be calculated from available specifications.

Illinois has 44 mapped data center facilities, of which only 6 operators have published power capacity figures totaling 236 MW. This campus ranks seventh among published capacity figures in the state, though this reflects the three-building Aurora campus aggregate rather than CHI3 alone, and most facilities in Illinois publish no figures at all.

Without a building-specific power figure, the significance of CHI3 to AI scaling cannot be read from its specifications. The 450,000 square feet is consistent with a mid-scale hyperscale building, which at typical AI densities of 40 kW per rack would support roughly 4,500 racks, but this remains an assumption about utilization rather than a fact about the facility's configuration.
